title: Scope the Claude sessions the SDK starts and the manager's tasks
notes:
Part 2 of 4 (after part 1 merges): scope the Claude sessions the SDK starts, and the manager's tasks.

- Main's sessions and worker screens' sessions (screen host, #226) start claude through the Agent SDK in chat-sessions.ts (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, ~line 344). Use the SDK's spawnClaudeCodeProcess hook to start it through scopedCommand(kind 'agent', the session's slot or pane id). First confirm the screen host's sessions go through this same code; if they start elsewhere, wrap that too.
- task-runner.ts (the manager's tasks across projects): scoped as 'agent' (they run builds and tests) under agents.slice, unit task-<slug>-<random>.
- Each scope's unit name recorded where card 3 and 4 can find it (the session's record).
- Remove these sites from the spawn guard's allowed count (lower, never raise).
Tests: the hook's argument building and the fallback, through the pure module. Hand check: main's claude and a worker screen's claude each in their own agent-*.scope. Docs: docs/processes, chat README, history.
Engineering bar: clean, testable, readable; decisions pure and tested, side effects thin.

comments.body: Shipped in #256: Claude screens' sessions (in the app and the screen host) run in agent-<session>-*.scope and the manager's tasks in task-<project>-*.scope under agents.slice, through one scoped spawn; task-runner.ts left the spawn guard. The unit is not recorded on the session or task yet (a re-attached screen-host session keeps its first unit).
Pull request #256 merged: Run Claude screens' sessions and the manager's tasks in their own systemd scopes https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/256
